record.paper_title: Models, feedback control, and open problems of 3D bipedal robotic walking
record.original_question: Design control methods that let a biped with passive feet or passive ankles stand stably and recover a quiescent standing posture after external pushes. The problem is specifically about balance recovery and stationary stabilization when the ankle is not actively actuated.

evidence.quote: Standing is challenging for robots with passive ankles. Regaining a quiescent standing position after being pushed is even harder.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a 3D bipedal robot modeled as a rigid multibody system whose feet (or ankles) are passive, i.e., the ankle joints supply no active torque and the foot–ground interaction is only a unilateral contact (the foot rolls or pivots freely about its support region subject to non-penetration and friction constraints). Let the joint configuration be q ∈ Q with actuated coordinates q_a (legs, hips, torso, arms) and unactuated coordinates q_u (the rigid-body pose modulo the contact and the passive ankle degrees of freedom), governed by the constrained Euler–Lagrange dynamics

    M(q) q̈ + C(q,q̇) q̇ + G(q) = B u + J(q)^T λ,

with contact wrench λ constrained to a friction cone and supported on the foot contact region, and B selecting only the actuated joints.

Design a feedback control law u = k(q, q̇) (possibly with internal state and hybrid switching among contact modes such as flat-foot, toe-roll, heel-roll, or stepping) such that:

(i) (Quiet stance) The closed-loop system admits an asymptotically stable equilibrium corresponding to a desired upright standing posture q* with q̇* = 0, while keeping the contact wrench inside the friction cone and the center of pressure within the support polygon.

(ii) (Push recovery) There exists a non-empty, characterizable set D of admissible external impulsive disturbances applied to the robot's body such that, for every disturbance in D, the closed-loop trajectory returns asymptotically to the quiescent standing posture q*, possibly after a finite number of automatic stepping or contact transitions, while maintaining all unilateral contact and friction constraints throughout.

Either exhibit such a controller together with a proof and an explicit characterization of the disturbance set D, or show that no such controller exists under the passive-ankle constraint.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of stable quiet standing and push recovery for bipeds with passive feet/ankles remains an active research topic. Recent work proposes partial solutions (e.g., whole-body locomotion control for passive-ankle robots, footstep-adjustment push recovery, series-elastic ankle reflex control), but no general controller with provable recovery guarantees for arbitrary admissible pushes on fully passive-ankle 3D bipeds has been established. The problem is therefore considered open in general, with partial results in restricted settings.

status_evidence.title: Dynamic locomotion for passive-ankle biped robots and humanoids using whole-body locomotion control
status_evidence.snippet: To date, whole-body control methods have not been employed for unsupported passive-ankle dynamic locomotion, leading researchers to devise new control approaches like WBLC.
status_evidence.claim: Passive-ankle stabilization is still an open methodological challenge being addressed by new controllers.

status_evidence.title: Push recovery for humanoid robots with passive damped ankles
status_evidence.snippet: Push recovery for humanoid robots with passive damped ankles.
status_evidence.claim: Active research targets push recovery specifically under passive-ankle conditions.

status_evidence.title: Footstep adjustment for biped push recovery on slippery surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Despite extensive studies on motion stabilization of bipeds, they are still limited by lack of disturbance coping capability.
status_evidence.claim: General push-recovery for bipeds is still acknowledged as an open problem.
